title: The Biggest Country With No Rivers
art_style: cute 2D vector sticker illustration, minimalist flat design, chibi proportions, flat colors with no gradients, muted earthy palette, clean dark outline, full body, centered, isolated on a solid plain white background, no text

scenes.narration: This is one of the biggest countries on Earth. And it doesn't have a single permanent river.
Saudi Arabia is bigger than Western Europe, but there's no river flowing all year.
It has wadis instead: dry valleys that only fill with water after rare storms.
In the south lies the Empty Quarter, the biggest continuous sand desert in the world.
So where does the water come from? Mostly, the sea.
Saudi Arabia makes about a fifth of all the desalinated water in the world, turning seawater into drinking water.
The rest comes from deep under the desert: ancient water, stored there since the Ice Age.
And here's the wild part. In the 1980s, Saudi Arabia used that water to grow wheat in the desert.

scenes.narration: These green circles are farms, watered by giant rotating sprinklers. You can see them from space.

scenes.narration: But that water doesn't refill. So the country stopped growing its own wheat.
A desert kingdom, running on seawater and ancient groundwater.
